abstract.text:
We argue that BPS ansatzes, entering manifestly vacuum BPS monopole solutions to equations of
motion in the (Minkowskian) non-Abelian Higgs model play the role of some electric form-factors and
that this implies (soft) violating the CP-invariance of the mentioned model, similar to taking place
in the Euclidian Yang-Mills (YM) theory with instantons, generating the θ-term in the appropriate
effective Hamiltonian.

predecessors.cited_work: M. K. Prasad, C. M. Sommerfeld, Phys. Rev. Lett. 35, 760 (1975); E. B. Bogomol’nyi, Yad. Fiz. 24, 449 (1976).

and YM sectors of the model (1.1).

dependence of the instanton models was analyzed in the paper [30], and we reconstruct partially the

arXiv:0812.5080v5[hep-th]4Dec2021
December 7, 2021

The principal goal of the present note is to show that BPS ansatzes f1BP S (r), f0BP S (r), one encounter
in the Higgs BPS monopole model, can serve as electric form-factors therein. Unlike this, electric form-
factors become trivial in the ’t Hooft-Polyakov theory [22, 23]. Grounding this fact will be the topic of
Section 2.
In Section 3 we show that presence of BPS ansatzes in the considered model implies violating the CP
invariance.

question.text: Do BPS ansatzes in the Minkowskian non-Abelian Higgs BPS monopole vacuum serve as electric form-factors, and does their presence imply CP violation?

sections.summary: The abstract states the central thesis: BPS ansatzes act as electric form-factors and softly violate CP, analogous to instanton θ-term physics. The introduction then sets up the Minkowskian Yang-Mills-Higgs model, the BPS limit, the Bogomol’nyi equation/bound, and the explicit vacuum BPS monopole solutions with their boundary behavior and topological properties.
sections.title: Thesis and BPS Limit Setup

sections.summary: The Bogomol’nyi equation is interpreted as a potentiality condition. The paper draws the helium-II superfluid analogy, invoking Landau critical velocity, potential motion, non-ideal gases, and Bose condensation. It then contrasts the ’t Hooft-Polyakov model, where the vacuum magnetic field and electric form-factors become trivial, and states the goal for Section 2.
sections.title: Potentiality, Superfluidity, and the ’t Hooft-Polyakov Contrast

sections.summary: This unit introduces the Dirac quantization condition, dyons, and the Zwanziger-Schwinger two-dyon generalization. It then computes the total angular momentum in a magnetic monopole background using the canonical momentum and ’t Hooft-Polyakov potentials, showing how Dirac quantization leads to a conserved total momentum J.
sections.title: Dirac Quantization and Monopole Angular Momentum

sections.summary: With the YM BPS ansatz present, the total momentum and isospin computation changes. The ansatz f1BPS screens the electric charge via e ↔ f1BPS e, making it an electric form-factor; f0BPS plays a similar role. The paper concludes that topologically nontrivial sectors become dyonic.
sections.title: BPS Ansatz as an Electric Form-Factor

sections.summary: The paper traces consequences of f1BPS(0) → 0. In zero topology, arbitrary magnetic charges near the origin lead to “magnons”; in nontrivial topology, an apparent UV divergence arises. Threads and magnetic-tension gaps produce a first-order phase transition, with the VEV of B² as order parameter, and the condition supports asymptotic freedom near the origin.
sections.title: Dyonic Sectors, Magnons, and Phase Transition

sections.summary: The Dirac-Zwanziger-Schwinger condition allows arbitrary electric charges for individual monopoles when only the difference is quantized. Adding CP conservation forces monopole electric charges to integer or half-integer multiples of e; without CP conservation, deviations from such charges are proportional to the strength of CP violation.
sections.title: CP Conservation and Monopole Charge Quantization

sections.summary: This unit introduces the instanton Yang-Mills effective Lagrangian with a θ-term. θ is treated as a quasimomentum; the equations of motion are unchanged. Quantization produces complex θ and imaginary topological momentum modes, leading to a non-separable Hilbert space and the no-go theorem for ordinary quantization methods.
sections.title: Instanton Theta-Term and Complex Theta Vacuum

sections.summary: The semi-classical analysis of dyons gives T(I+E)=2πn. At θ=0, q=ne; at θ≠0, q=ne−θe/2π, so no electrically neutral magnetic monopole exists. In the monopole sector, θ dependence differs from instanton tunneling, and CP violation—regardless of mechanism—can induce a linear term in I+E and noninteger charges.
sections.title: Semi-Classical Dyon Charge under Theta and CP Violation

sections.summary: Dirac fundamental quantization resolves the Gauss law via topological Dirac variables and vacuum electric monopoles. The rotary action W_N has a purely real P_N spectrum and is both P- and C-invariant, unlike the instanton θ case whose energy is linear in e and θ. The paper concludes CP conservation in the BPS-monopole YMH model.
sections.title: Dirac Quantization and CP Conservation in the BPS Monopole Vacuum
